name: Edinburgh
tagline: A castle on a volcano and closes to explore
summary: The medieval Old Town and Georgian New Town face each other across a valley, so most sights are a walk apart. Climb Arthur's Seat on your clearest day.
seasonNote: August festivals triple prices and crowds; Hogmanay at New Year is another peak.
arrival: Trams and the Airlink 100 bus reach the centre in about 30 minutes.
gettingAround: Walk, but expect hills and stairs; Lothian buses take contactless payment.
cashTip: Contactless cards work everywhere; Scottish banknotes are valid UK pounds.
foodTip: Try haggis with neeps and tatties, Cullen skink, Scottish salmon and a whisky tasting.
buyTip: Tartan and cashmere from mills with Scottish labels, whisky and shortbread.
baseArea: Old Town, New Town or Stockbridge

connections.note: Direct LNER and Lumo trains to King's Cross; book ahead.
Air time only; add airport transfers.

items.name: Edinburgh Castle
items.summary: A fortress on a volcanic crag, holding Scotland's crown jewels and the Stone of Destiny.
items.expect: Timed tickets that sell out in summer; windy and exposed.
items.tip: Book the first slot and be there for the One o'Clock Gun.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate per adult in local currency, not a live ticket quote; check current prices and what is included.

whyVisit: A fortress on a volcanic crag, holding Scotland's crown jewels and the Stone of Destiny.

items.name: Arthur's Seat
items.summary: An extinct volcano in the middle of the city, with a 251-metre summit.
items.expect: A real hill walk of 45 to 60 minutes up; rocky and windy on top.
items.tip: Wear proper shoes and take the gentler path from Dunsapie Loch if unsure.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate per adult in local currency, not a live ticket quote; check current prices and what is included.
items.sourceNote: Editorial selection. Durations, spending allowances and itinerary advice are planning estimates; check opening days and prices with the venue before you go.
whyVisit: An extinct volcano in the middle of the city, with a 251-metre summit.
The summit view covers the city, the sea and the hills beyond.
visitFlow: Climb to the summit and come down past the crags.
items.bestFor: Visitors interested in landscapes and wildlife and big views
tradeoffs: A real hill walk of 45 to 60 minutes up; rocky and windy on top.
